who.value: Buyer browsing a category, e.g. Fashion

job.value: Browse or search within a category cluster

arrivedFrom.value: A category link in the top nav (e.g. 'Fashion')

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The 'Women's Fashion / Men's Fashion' tabs and 'Shop by category' show it's Fashion, but the hero headline 'Every kinda thing, for every kinda person' is generic and doesn't name the category.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The hero 'Search for anything' bar is prominent, but a second search bar ('Search for an item') sits directly above it in the nav, so two equal searches compete.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Search', the Trending terms and the Women's/Men's Fashion tabs all say what they do.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: Nothing beyond plain shopping terms like 'Trending' and 'Shop by category'.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: The only choices are what to search or which sub-category to tap.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: The first screen is hero, tabs and category tiles; deeper rows come later down the page.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Hero search, trending terms and category tiles all serve browsing.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Images, tabs and one search field carry the screen; the only text is a headline and a trending line.
